function.name: crash_list
function.description: List every crash report, one line each: its ID, fingerprint, how many times it happened, the version that crashed, the function inside remind where it happened, and the panic message, cut short. Reports with the same fingerprint usually share a cause, but check. Start here.

function.name: crash_read
function.description: Read one crash report: when and how often it happened, the panic, the request being served, and the stack. By default the stack shows only remind's own frames, with file and line; set full for every frame. Log lines are in crash_logs.

id.description: a report ID from crash_list, such as cr_1e2ea0

full.description: show every stack frame, not just remind's

function.name: crash_search
function.description: Search every crash report for text, ignoring case: panic messages, request paths and bodies, stacks, and log lines. Lists each match with the report's ID and where it was found.

query.description: text to look for, such as a function name, a path, or words from a panic

function.name: crash_logs
function.description: Read the log lines remind wrote just before a crash.

id.description: a report ID from crash_list, such as cr_1e2ea0

function.name: crash_goroutines
function.description: Summarize the goroutine dump of a stuck request: goroutines with identical stacks are grouped and counted, so a dump of thousands reads as a few groups. Use it for reports of kind stuck.

id.description: a report ID from crash_list, such as cr_1e2ea0

function.name: code_list
function.description: List the files under a directory of remind's source, with how many lines each has. Use it to find your way around; use code_search to find where something is defined.

dir.description: a directory such as "store"; empty lists everything

function.name: code_read
function.description: Read part of a file of remind's source, with line numbers. Shows at most 200 lines at a time; ask for a range with start and end. Read a file before you change it.

path.description: a file path, such as store/store.go

start.description: the first line to show; default 1

end.description: the last line to show; default 200 lines after start

function.name: code_search
function.description: Search remind's Go files for a regular expression and list the matching lines with file and line number. Use it to find where a function is defined or called.

pattern.description: a Go regular expression, such as func \(s \*Store\) Get

dir.description: limit the search to this directory

function.name: run_tests
function.description: Run go test on remind's code, as it is now, and report failed tests, build errors, and each package's result. Run one package while you work; run ./... before you finish.

package.description: a package pattern, such as ./store or ./...

run.description: run only tests matching this regular expression, such as ^TestGetDeleted$

function.name: code_patch
function.description: Change a file by replacing one piece of text, or create a new file, such as a test, by leaving old empty. Read a file with code_read before changing it, and copy old exactly from what you read. After a change, the package and its tests are compiled, and you see the result.

path.description: the file to change, such as store/store.go

old.description: text copied exactly from the file, appearing in it once; empty to create a new file

new.description: the text to put in its place, or the new file's contents

function.name: issue_search
function.description: Search the open issues in the issue tracker, by words or by fingerprint; with neither, list them all. Issues that contain more of the words come first. Check here before filing, since a crash may already be filed, perhaps by a person, with no fingerprint and in other words.

query.description: words to look for in titles and bodies, such as parseBearer index out of range

function.name: issue_file
function.description: File a new issue for a crash group, once you know its cause. Search the open issues first; don't file a problem that is already filed. File one issue per cause.

title.description: one line naming the problem, such as "store.Get returns a deleted reminder"

body.description: the cause, the evidence, the fix, and the reports it covers

fingerprint.description: the crash group's fingerprint, from crash_list

function.name: issue_comment
function.description: Add a comment to an issue, such as new crash reports that match one already filed.

body.description: the comment, such as new reports of the same crash

function.name: submit_diagnosis
function.description: Finish the job: submit one diagnosis per crash group. Call it once, at the end, after filing an issue for each new cause. For status fixed, the reproducer test must fail on the original code and pass on yours; this is checked.

groups.description: one entry per crash group; every report belongs to exactly one

reports.description: the IDs of every report in the group

root_cause.description: where the code is wrong, which may not be where it crashed

file.description: a file path, such as store/store.go

function.description: a function or method, such as (*Store).Get or TestGetDeleted

evidence.description: why this is the cause: what you read and ran

reproducer.description: the test you wrote that fails before the fix; leave out for already_fixed and duplicate

file.description: a file path, such as store/store.go

function.description: a function or method, such as (*Store).Get or TestGetDeleted

fix.description: what you changed, for status fixed

issue.description: the issue you filed, for status fixed or needs_human

duplicate.description: for status duplicate: the open issue it duplicates

message.content: Now the API layer. Let me read `api/reminders.go`, `auth/auth.go`, and `api/api.go`.
message.reasoning:
Interesting. Let me analyze:

1. **duration.Parse** (duration/duration.go:29): `s[len(s)-1]` panics on empty string with "index out of range [-1]". Request body `{"for":""}` — the snooze handler parses an empty duration. Root cause: duration.Parse doesn't handle empty string. Fix: return error if s == "". Also, there's another latent bug: `rest[i]` after digits — if rest ends with digits... wait, the first check ensures the last char is not a digit, so rest[i] after digits always has a unit char? Hmm: loop: i counts digits; if i==0 error; unit := units[rest[i]] — if rest[i] is out of range (i == len(rest)), that would panic too. But the initial check (last char not a digit) guarantees digits are followed by a non-digit... Actually wait: "1h30" — last char '0' is a digit → error. "1h3" → error. So digits at the end are rejected upfront. But what about `rest[i]` where i is digits count and rest[i] exists — yes since last char isn't a digit, any digit run is followed by something. OK. But also `rest = rest[i+1:]` — if rest[i] is the last char, rest[i+1:] is fine (empty). So the only bug is empty string. Also negative numbers "-5m"? i==0 → error "expected a number". OK.

So fix duration.Parse: `if s == "" { return 0, fmt.Errorf("duration %q: empty", s) }`. Hmm, but where did the empty come from? api/reminders.go:197 calls duration.Parse with the "for" field from body {"for":""}. The API handler probably doesn't validate empty. The root cause could be argued in duration.Parse (crashes there) — Parse should reject empty input with an error rather than panic. I'd fix Parse. Maybe also the handler should validate, but fixing Parse is the minimal correct fix. The reproducer test: TestParseEmpty in duration package — fails on current code (panics) and passes after fix.

2. **store.List** (store/store.go:135-136): `end := min(offset+limit, len(out))` then `out[offset:end]`. If offset > len(out), then out[offset:end] panics. [20:2]: offset=20, len(out)=2? Then end=min(20+limit?, 2)... wait high=2 means end=2, so offset+limit ≥ 2... offset=20 > end=2 → panic "slice bounds out of range [20:2]". Yes. With len(out)=1 → [20:1]. So two users had 2 and 1 non-deleted reminders, requesting offset=20. Fix: clamp offset: if offset >= len(out) return nil, or `if offset > len(out) { offset = len(out) }`... Actually simplest: 
```go
if offset >= len(out) { return nil }
end := min(offset+limit, len(out))
return out[offset:end]
```
Or clamp offset before slicing. Note limit could also be negative → end = min(offset+limit, len) could be < offset... if limit negative, e.g., offset=0, limit=-5 → end=-5 → panic [0:-5]. Also offset negative → out[-5:end] panics. Where do offset/limit come from? api/reminders.go:127 listReminders parses query params. Let me read that. The fix in store.List should handle offset < 0? Maybe clamp both. Let me check the API to see how offset/limit are parsed — maybe they're clamped there but the store should be robust. I'll read api/reminders.go.

3. **api.(*API).owned** (api/reminders.go:144): nil pointer. Let me read api/reminders.go around 130-200.

4. **export/stats nil pointer** (api/users.go:104, 117): `u := auth.UserFrom(r.Context())` — if UserFrom returns nil (e.g., user deleted?), then u.ID deref panics. Wait but both crashes are at line 104 and 117, which are `a.Store.List(u.ID, ...)` — hmm, line 104 is `rems := a.Store.List(u.ID, 0, 1000)`. The deref of u would happen at `u.ID` on that line. So u is nil → auth.UserFrom returned nil. Interesting: both requests came from the Safari user agent (usr_ana?). Wait — closeAccount at 14:12? No, DELETE rem_0003 was the delete. Hmm.

Wait, actually the logs show DELETE /v1/reminders/rem_0003 at 14:12:35. The done crash at 14:15 was for rem_0003 which was deleted → Get returns (nil, ErrNotFound) and owned dereferenced it.

For export (14:20) and stats (14:16): the user agent is the Safari one (usr_ana). Maybe usr_ana closed their account? The logs don't show a closeAccount call... The log lines are only 7 and cut? "log lines: 7; read them with crash_logs" — we saw 7 lines. No account closure logged. Hmm, but maybe auth.UserFrom returns nil when... Let me read auth/auth.go and see how UserFrom works and when the context user could be missing.

Actually wait — maybe these are different: for export and stats, maybe `a.Store.List` is fine but something else is nil... The stack says crash at api/users.go:104 (export) and 117 (stats). Line 104: `rems := a.Store.List(u.ID, 0, 1000)` — derefs u (nil). Line 117: `for _, rem := range a.Store.List(u.ID, 0, 1000)` — derefs u. Hmm wait, line 117 in my read: `for _, rem := range a.Store.List(u.ID, 0, 1000) {`. Yes.

But hold on — could it be that `a.Store.List` panics due to the same offset bug? No, offset=0, limit=1000: out[0:min(1000, len)] fine. Nil deref is u.

So why would u be nil? auth.UserFrom(r.Context()) returns nil if the context doesn't have the user. Let me read auth/auth.go. Maybe Require puts user only when token valid, and these requests had valid tokens... Both crashes: same Safari UA. Maybe the user usr_ana closed their account — but no log. Hmm, maybe DeleteUser removes the user from store but auth middleware reads user from store by token at request time and returns nil if the user no longer exists? Let me read auth.

Actually — maybe UserFrom returns nil when the token maps to a deleted user. The middleware might do: look up token → user; if not found, still call next with no user in context? Then handlers deref nil. But then me() would also crash... me() derefs u too.

Let me read auth/auth.go and api/api.go to understand routing and middleware.

Also the two "deleted reminder" crashes: owned at api/reminders.go:144. Let me read api/reminders.go fully.

And listReminders at 127 for offset parsing.
